answer: Each bonded identity posts collateral that can be slashed when evidence proves equivocation. If k identities coordinate the same conflicting votes, correlated penalties grow as O(k^2), so splitting control across a swarm does not divide the risk. Detection applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation makes recovery harder. A shared control thread can leave a mirror-like evidence trail across the canyon of identities, exposing coordination rather than concealing it.
